raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #44973
* #44972
* #44971
* #44970
* #44969
* #43326
* #43325
* #43171
* __->__ #43170
* #43168

Current head `2509d740d3`, based on main `47eeddcd18`. Stack predecessor: #43168. This PR targets `main` after its stack predecessor merged.

## Motivation

`UnifiedSWAAllocatorBase` (`--enable-unified-memory` with a hybrid sliding-window model) filtered every segment free by swa liveness with a boolean mask (`reps[swa_v2p > 0]`). A mask index runs `nonzero`, which copies its count to the host and blocks the scheduler until the in-flight forward drains, so under the overlap scheduler the next batch is prepared only after the GPU went idle. In gpt-oss-20b serving traces (SM90, page size 256) the free of tokens that left the window (`free_swa_segment`) and the request release (`_release_page_reps` at `free_group_end`) issued about 2.6 such syncs per prefill. Prefill cycles ran +1.3..+3.3% (speculative) and +2.5..+7.0% (non-speculative) longer than with the paged SWA allocator at matched batch size, all of it GPU idle.

## Modifications

Two-pool allocation reclaim flushes the deferred FULL-only segment queue before sizing eviction. A regression test fills that queue alone and verifies allocation succeeds without evicting the tree.

The paged SWA allocator frees the same segments with a fixed shape: its callers split a kv row by host bookkeeping, and it trusts that split. The unified callers make the same split: `free_kv_row_segments` sends `[swa_dead_lo, swa_evicted_seqlen)` through `free_full_segment`, the tree picks `FreeDeviceKV` or `FreeDeviceKVFullOnly` per node, and the out-of-window free releases only tokens above `swa_dead_lo`, with a cursor that only moves up. So `free_swa_segment` and `free_segment` now free every page they are handed on the swa side, and `free_full_segment` releases the full side only, through its own deferred list for the free group (`full_free_group`), which `flush_deferred_full_frees` also drains when Mamba state needs memory. Each checks its premise with `expect`, as the paged allocator's `swa.peer_mapped` does: asynchronous, and loud from `SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK=warn` up. The two invariants are declared in `allocator/swa.py` beside the paged allocator's: the registry refuses a name it already holds, and a test fixture that patches `sys.modules` makes the next test import `unified_hybrid_swa` again. Page size 1 takes the same path. The set-shaped `free()` and `free_swa()` keep their filter; `RecoverSWAWithLockedFull` relies on it.

A second out-of-window free over the same range was filtered to a no-op. No caller issues one; under strict checks it is now reported instead.

Tests (CPU):
- `test_segment_frees_dispatch_no_data_dependent_shape` records, with a `TorchDispatchMode`, every op whose output shape depends on values (a boolean-mask index, `nonzero`, `unique`, `item`). Before: three mask indexes at page size 1 and at 4. After: none, and both sides' capacity comes back.
- `test_a_double_ratchet_is_reported` (replaces `test_double_ratchet_is_filtered_not_crashed`) and `test_a_full_only_free_of_a_bound_swa_page_is_reported` fail before (nothing raises) and pass after.
- The test that reclaims full-attention KV for Mamba state (on a model with both Mamba state and sliding-window layers) and the eviction fixture name the new list.
- `test_importing_the_module_again_registers_nothing_twice` runs the module again as such a fixture does: a duplicate-invariant error before, none after (`test_lmcache_component_cursors.py` errors in 3 of its 4 cases with the invariants in `unified_hybrid_swa` and passes with them in `allocator/swa.py`).
- The unified-memory CPU tests pass with `SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK=2` exactly as without it, so none of them frees an already released sliding-window page through a segment free.

## Accuracy Tests

Earlier combined stack `b550cacde6` adds a test-fixture correction in #43326: the Gemma4 read-stream fixture declares its FULL address space, and the HiSparse registry test uses real `CacheInitParams` for the retained-window calculation. Both complete test files pass locally with GPUs hidden: 4 Gemma4 tests and 26 registry tests. Pre-commit passed. The five descendant patches are unchanged (`git range-diff`); this follow-up changes no production code. The earlier 455-test run did not cover these two files; GitHub CI has not yet been revalidated for this head.

Validation before the test-fixture follow-up, on combined stack `4cf27a551c`: 455 tests and 921 subtests passed on B300, plus the two widened-history regressions against Rust TreeCore. The new FULL-fallback metadata cases cover eager execution and CUDA graph replay. New allocation-reclaim, explicit-prefill and JIT-reuse regressions fail on the previous code and pass with the fixes. These are combined-stack checks, not independent model reruns of each PR.

The measurements in this section are historical results from before this rebase, at the revisions/configurations stated below. Current combined-stack validation is linked above.

SM90, TP1, gpt-oss-20b, no speculation, radix cache, overlap scheduler, CUDA graphs on, `--mem-fraction-static 0.8`. Baseline: the default pool. Unified: `--enable-unified-memory`. Every server ran with the per-step pool checks and the allocator invariants on (`SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_BUSY=1 SGLANG_CHECK_KV_PAGE_INVARIANTS=1 SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK=1`), so a free that this change gets wrong stops the server or is reported. These ran on this commit over main 7224fce1b5. GSM8K, all 1314 test questions, 5-shot, greedy:

| page size | backend | baseline | unified |
|---|---|---|---|
| 256 | triton | 0.502 | 0.515 |
| 256 | fa3 | 0.553 | 0.558 |
| 1 | triton | 0.533 | 0.536 |
| 1 | fa3 | 0.566 | 0.535 |

gpt-oss-20b's GSM8K score moves by several points between identical runs (up to ~6 in our runs of one configuration), and three of the four rows favour the unified pool.

Under the same checks, two load tests at page size 256: one with a shared prefix (one 4096-token system prompt, 192 requests with 128-token questions and 2048 output tokens, concurrency 192) and one with long outputs (100 requests, 512 input / 4096 output tokens, concurrency 128). Every request completed on both arms and both backends, and no server reported a leak, double free, invariant violation or illegal memory access.

GPU unit tests for unified memory: 4104 passed, 0 failed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The measurements in this section are historical results from before this rebase, at the revisions/configurations stated below. Current combined-stack validation is linked above.

`bench_serving` with random prompts at concurrency 64, in two shapes: 2048 input / 512 output tokens (200 prompts) and 8192 input / 64 output tokens (100 prompts). gpt-oss-20b, no speculation, page size 256, radix cache, overlap scheduler, CUDA graphs on, `--mem-fraction-static 0.55`. Each entry is the unified pool's gap to the default pool on the same tree, before (main) and after this PR; the default pool runs twice and the gap is against the mean of the two runs, with their spread (A/A) as the noise floor. This table ran on this commit over an earlier main.

| backend | shape | req/s, main -> this PR | mean TTFT | mean E2E | A/A (req/s / TTFT / E2E) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fa3 | 2048 / 512 | -1.4% -> -0.7% | +18.2% -> -0.0% | +1.5% -> +0.8% | 0.6 / 0.3 / 0.7 |
| fa3 | 8192 / 64 | -1.1% -> -0.6% | +7.2% -> +0.5% | +1.2% -> +0.6% | 0.8 / 2.1 / 0.8 |
| triton | 2048 / 512 | -0.9% -> -0.1% | +14.9% -> -0.3% | +1.0% -> +0.1% | 0.3 / 0.1 / 0.4 |
| triton | 8192 / 64 | -5.0% -> -0.3% | +8.3% -> +0.5% | +5.4% -> +0.3% | 0.4 / 0.2 / 0.4 |

The triton rows compare with the first default-pool run only, and their A/A is main's: on this PR's tree the second run compiled kernels during the benchmark. On prefill batches with identical new and cached token counts in both arms' logs, unified prefill throughput is 1.000 (fa3) and 0.999 (triton) of the default pool's with this PR, with an interquartile range of 0.996-1.003; on main the median is 0.997 with an interquartile range of 0.920-1.065, the spread the host syncs add.

The same configuration on this commit over main 7224fce1b5, unified pool against the default pool:

| backend | shape | req/s | mean TTFT | mean E2E | A/A (req/s / TTFT / E2E) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fa3 | 2048 / 512 | -0.3% | +0.2% | +0.4% | 0.1 / 0.6 / 0.1 |
| fa3 | 8192 / 64 | -0.2% | +0.4% | +0.2% | 0.1 / 0.6 / 0.2 |
| triton | 2048 / 512 | +0.7% | +0.2% | -0.6% | 1.6 / 0.6 / 1.4 |
| triton | 8192 / 64 | -2.2% | -0.2% | +2.2% | 3.9 / 0.8 / 4.0 |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body:
**[bug]** Two-pool `evict_to_free_tokens` still flushes the old 3-tuple, so this new list is invisible there.

`_flush_deferred_free_group` returns when `not any(pending_groups)`. After this change, `free_full_segment` queues into `full_page_reps_group` instead of `free_page_reps_group` (or `full_free_group` at page size 1). A group that only has those full-only segment frees is treated as empty on the two-pool path (`UnifiedSWAAllocatorBase.evict_to_free_tokens`) and left queued, so `reclaim_plan` can over-evict or fail while the pages are already waiting to be released. The tri-pool override goes through this method and is fine; gpt-oss is two-pool.

**Suggestion:** Pass `self.full_page_reps_group` in the two-pool tuple as well, or share one pending-groups helper with this flush.

@@ -1724,7 +1735,12 @@ def flush_deferred_full_frees(self) -> None:
         """Expose grouped composite frees while preserving the group scope."""
         _flush_deferred_free_group(
             self,
-            (self.free_group, self.free_page_reps_group, self.full_free_group),
+            (
+                self.free_group,
+                self.free_page_reps_group,
+                self.full_page_reps_group,

 _SWA_PEER_MAPPED = Invariant("swa.peer_mapped", Bucket.FATAL_UNCONTAINABLE, IsTrue())
 # free_full leaves the mapping alone, so a live entry would strand its SWA peer.
 _SWA_PEER_RELEASED = Invariant("swa.peer_released", Bucket.GUARD, IsTrue())
+# The unified allocator's segment frees trust the caller's bound/released split.
+UNIFIED_SWA_SEGMENT_BOUND = Invariant(

+)
+UNIFIED_SWA_SEGMENT_RELEASED = Invariant(

+)

 from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.base import MambaFullCacheDonor
-from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.swa import SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.swa import (
+    UNIFIED_SWA_SEGMENT_BOUND,
+    UNIFIED_SWA_SEGMENT_RELEASED,
+    SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator,
+)

     FloatMultiEndedAllocator,
     MultiEndedAllocator,
@@ -41,6 +45,7 @@

 from sglang.srt.utils.common import get_num_new_pages
+from sglang.srt.utils.invariants import expect
 from sglang.srt.utils.rank_consensus_checker import rank_consensus
 
 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
@@ -172,6 +177,7 @@ def __init__(
 
         self.free_group = None
         self.free_page_reps_group: Optional[List[torch.Tensor]] = None
+        self.full_page_reps_group: List[torch.Tensor] = []
         self.full_free_group: List[torch.Tensor] = []
         # Empty (not None) for the leak checker.
         self.free_pages = torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
@@ -612,27 +618,25 @@ def free_swa(self, free_index: torch.Tensor) -> None:
         self.swa_attn_allocator.clear_inverse_history()
 
     def free_swa_segment(self, free_index: torch.Tensor, *, start_pos: int) -> None:
-        """free_swa() for a kv-row segment: `start_pos` promises a contiguous
-        ascending range, so page reps come from stride arithmetic, not `torch.unique`."""
+        """free_swa() for a kv-row segment whose swa pages are all bound: page reps
+        come from `start_pos`, so it is fixed-shape at every page size."""
         if free_index is None or free_index.numel() == 0:
             return
-        if self.page_size == 1:
-            self.free_swa(free_index)
-            return
-        ps = self.page_size
         reps = self.swa_attn_allocator._page_reps(
             free_index.detach().to(torch.int64), start_pos
         )
-        # Keep only pages still bound on swa; freeing a tombstoned one would
-        # corrupt the hole list. `> 0` strict: -1 tombstoned, 0 padding sink.
-        rep_pages = reps // ps
-        swa_v2p_pages = self.swa_attn_allocator.virtual_to_physical[rep_pages]
-        live_reps = reps[swa_v2p_pages > 0]
-        if live_reps.numel() == 0:

inline_comments.body:
**[bug]** Two-pool `evict_to_free_tokens` still flushes the old 3-tuple, so this new list is invisible there.

`_flush_deferred_free_group` returns when `not any(pending_groups)`. After this change, `free_full_segment` queues into `full_page_reps_group` instead of `free_page_reps_group` (or `full_free_group` at page size 1). A group that only has those full-only segment frees is treated as empty on the two-pool path (`UnifiedSWAAllocatorBase.evict_to_free_tokens`) and left queued, so `reclaim_plan` can over-evict or fail while the pages are already waiting to be released. The tri-pool override goes through this method and is fine; gpt-oss is two-pool.

**Suggestion:** Pass `self.full_page_reps_group` in the two-pool tuple as well, or share one pending-groups helper with this flush.
